chapter: Memphis, Oklahoma, the Kirk band and Kansas City
title: Piney Brown's place, Joe Turner and Martha Raye in Kansas City
summary: After their nightly work the band went to Piney Brown's, where Joe Turner, Pete Johnson and Hot Lips Page played, and Martha Raye, on her way to Hollywood, stayed to sing.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Now was this part of the period when you were playing mostly in Kansas City, you had a chance to live there? I mean, you were part of the musical life in Kansas City?
Oh, yes, a great part of it. Without me - oh, that was terrific, especially when we were in the park.

We worked every night from 9 till 12 and during the summer Tiny Brown's place was open. That's where Joe - the blues singer - Joe Turner and Pete Johnson were working. John would drive by and drop the boys off there and I'd go home and change from my sweaty outfit, take a bath. Oh, one thing I want to tell you. When we passed the place we'd hear "Georgia Brown". I'd go home, take a bath and dress and put on something cool and come back and they were still playing "Georgia Brown". But Hot Lips Page and about 15 musicians would come in and there was such a terrific arrangement that you'd just pull your hair out. Martha Raye was on her way - she was around 18 years old, I think they said - was on her way to make a movie in Hollywood. It cost them, they said, a million dollars or more wiring and sending for her and she don't want to leave. She had such a ball. She just stayed there. She used to come up and sing every night. I'm telling you, those sessions were something else!
Who were some of the people? You mentioned Hot Lips Page. Do you want to stop a minute and think?
The Sunset Cafe, and when Martha came through?
Was she already famous at that point?
No. I think they said she was 18 years old.
